artifacts.synopsis: TE Michael Woodham complained that South Florida Presbytery erred by excommunicating a Teaching Elder it had previously deposed without first assigning him to membership in a particular church as required by BCO 46-8. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that Presbytery retained jurisdiction over a deposed minister until transfer to a local church was completed, and that Presbytery's efforts to implement BCO 46-8 showed no clear error; two concurring opinions (RE Donahoe and RE Eggert) offered alternative reasoning regarding the scope of Presbytery's residual jurisdiction.

artifacts.synopsis: Great Lakes Presbytery erred in approving Recommendation 5 of its Judicial Commission's report, which preemptively stated that Presbytery would not recommend or transfer TE Gonzales if he declined to demit or step away from ministry, because such action exceeded Presbytery's authority apart from censure after due judicial process.

artifacts.title: Lee v. Korean Eastern Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Korean Eastern Presbytery erred in dismissing TE Eliot Lee's charges against two Teaching Elders without conducting a trial; the SJC held that once properly drawn charges are filed, a Presbytery must proceed to adjudicate them unless it can demonstrate specific constitutional grounds for dismissal, and remanded the matter to KEP.

artifacts.title: Certification of presbytery dismissal by committee chairman's letter

matches.evidence: A letter from a presbytery committee chairman is insufficient evidence of dismissal; BCO 46-6 requires a certificate bearing the stated clerk's signature per BCO 10-4.

artifacts.title: Sufficiency of faith profession for visible church membership

matches.evidence: CCB found proposed overtures conflicting with BCO because the only required profession for church membership is faith in Jesus Christ, with the session judging qualifications.

artifacts.title: Proposed membership-transfer vows misusing 'profession of faith'

matches.evidence: A Southeast Alabama overture adding transfer-of-membership procedures was in conflict because it equated 'profession of faith' with doctrinal subscription and contained internal procedural contradictions.
